description: A stereo echo delay whose time can be tapped in or taken from a clock, with a send and return in its feedback path

params.text: Plays what is in the delay line backwards
Holds what is in the delay line, repeating it and letting no new signal in
How much of the delayed signal is fed back into the delay line
The level of the signal going into the delay
The balance between the dry signal and the repeats
Sends the repeats alternately to the left and the right output

inputs.text: The left return back into the feedback path
The right return back into the feedback path
A CV changing the delay time
A CV changing the input level
A clock here sets the delay time from the interval between its pulses
A pulse switches the reverse playing on and off
A pulse switches the hold on and off

outputs.text: The left send out of the feedback path
The right send out of the feedback path

notes: the input level, the feedback and the delay time are set by dragging their red displays; the green display beside each shows the value once its CV input has been added
three taps on the tap button are needed before a delay time is worked out from them
holding the Command or Windows key while dragging the time display moves the window being read out of the buffer while HOLD is on, and turns the display yellow
the delay line holds 180 seconds of stereo at 48kHz, and half that at 96kHz
menu: Delay CV Input Mapping Modes — sets how the voltage at the time CV input maps onto the delay time, as Old style mode, Exponential mode, Inverse Exponential mode, Logaritmic mode or Linear mode
